options.title: Implement a wait-time threshold escalation huddle

options.how_we_would_know: By tracking the frequency and outcomes of the escalation huddles, we can assess their impact on reducing wait times and improving patient care. Feedback from patients and staff can also provide valuable insights into the effectiveness of this intervention.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the escalation huddles fail to consistently reduce wait times or if more systemic issues are identified, we should reconsider the approach and explore alternative solutions.

options.title: Review and adjust bed allocation practices
options.description: Review the current bed allocation practices and guidelines. Adjust these practices to ensure that reserve monitored beds are protected for acute arrivals, especially CTAS 1 and CTAS 2 patients.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: This option may shift pressure to the nursing leadership and bed allocation team, as they will be responsible for implementing and monitoring the revised bed allocation practices. However, the local context of high bed occupancy and long room-to-physician times may limit the effectiveness of this option if the underlying causes are not addressed simultaneously.
options.how_we_would_know: By tracking bed occupancy rates and the proportion of CTAS 1 and CTAS 2 patients receiving immediate access to monitored beds, we can assess the effectiveness of the revised bed allocation practices. Regular audits and feedback from relevant staff can also provide insights into the impact of these changes.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the revised bed allocation practices fail to consistently provide immediate access to monitored beds for CTAS 1 and CTAS 2 patients, or if more fundamental issues are identified, we should reconsider the approach and explore alternative solutions.
